title: Exceptional coefficient construction: system transport
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ with $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $R_E$, uniformizers $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=R_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed separated over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For $T=X,\overline X,Y$ use the ordinary derived category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_{E,n})_T$-modules on its etale or pro-etale site; exactness is levelwise. Normalization means invertibility of every derived transition-adjoint [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Let $C_T=\nu^*_{T,A}$, $V_T=R\nu_{T,A,*}$ and $\mathsf F^{et}=Rp_{c,A,*}j_{!,A}$. On bounded-below systems with etale-origin levels, $C_T\dashv V_T$ restricts to an equivalence preserving normalization, with its actual system unit and counit. The proper/open comparison
$$C_Y\mathsf F^{et}V_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf F^{pro},\qquad \mathsf F^{pro}=Rp_{c,A,*}^{pro}j_{!,A}^{pro},$$
is the canonical derived proper mate followed by termwise open comparison. There is an exact $R_E$-linear adjunction
$$\mathsf F^{pro}\dashv\mathsf G^{pro}=C_X\mathsf G^{et}V_Y$$
on this class, transported from the ordinary etale system adjunction. Its evaluation isomorphisms identify its finite operations, units, counits and quotient transitions with the finite transported adjunction and its counit-normalized coefficient transposes. The right functor preserves bounded-below normalization and has a lower bound independent of $n$. The adjunction and comparison maps exist in the derived category of systems before evaluation; no faithfulness of evaluation on morphisms is asserted.

source.place: Propositions 2.23, 2.29, 3.16; Section 5, especially Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24; blueprint exceptional inverse-image construction. Specific obligation: returned construction steps 8–9, preserved verbatim in the delivery report.

proof.text: Obtain the ordinary etale support package S and exceptional adjunction G from the existing etale system-adjoint theorem. Retain its common lower bound and normalization clause.

Construct the three comparison packages at the fixed evaluations PX, PY and PZ, with bounded-origin equivalences, finite actual units/counits, finite inverse origins and preservation of origin by evaluation.

Construct the pro-etale proper/open operation P and canonical mate R; obtain the comparison isomorphism, system and finite left stability, finite right bounds and the comparison evaluation equation. Compose with the source site counit and use directBound to prove originComparisonIso.

Construct the system and finite origin adjunctions by a natural chain of actual Hom equivalences. Its final equivalence sends u to the inverse source counit followed by C_X(u); its inverse sends k to V_X(k) followed by the inverse site unit. Prove mutual inverses by triangles, left and right naturality, then apply Adjunction.mkOfHomEquiv. Its Hom formula gives the required transpose equation after cancelling the source counit. Right stability follows from the bound of G, directBound and inverseOrigin; finite stability follows from the supplied finite bound.

Equip the two actual pro-etale functors with the canonical additive, shift, triangulated and scalar structures. Apply the origin-adjunction evaluation theorem to the constructed record and its finite source counits. This yields its evaluated units, counits and quotient-transition word.

Prove normalization by directNormalized for V_Y, the normalized clause of G, and inverseNormalized for C_X. Prove the common lower bound by composing directBound, the fixed bound of G and inverseBound. Assemble the twelve coherence clauses into ExceptionalSystemTransport.
